payload.name: Preserve stated attributes of recommendations
payload.description: When a speaker recommends or mentions an item with an explicitly stated attribute or reason, use this during extraction and CRUD to keep that qualifier in the memory candidate and in the stored memory.
content: During extraction, if the source states a recommendation together with an explicit attribute or reason (e.g., 'X is calming and cute', 'Y is great for beginners'), record that qualifier as part of the candidate content instead of reducing the item to a bare name in a list.

During UPDATE or MERGE, when an existing memory already covers the recommended item, merge the stated attribute onto that item and keep the evidence link; do not overwrite the memory with a summary that omits the attribute.
Only preserve qualifiers the speaker explicitly linked to the item; do not add inferred attributes, and do not list every adjective when the speaker did not attach it to the recommendation.

solves: Construction summarization often drops explicitly stated attributes or reasons attached to a recommended item, so later questions about that attribute fail. This Skill applies when a speaker pairs a recommendation with a stated qualifier (e.g., 'calming and cute', 'great for beginners') and the extraction candidate would otherwise list the item without that qualifier. It does not apply when no attribute is stated or when the attribute is inferred rather than explicitly spoken by the speaker.
